domain: Technology Governance / Information Epistemology / Digital Forensics
topic_summary: Analysis of the deepfake detection crisis through the experience of Hany Farid, the world's leading digital forensics expert, who reports he can no longer trust his own eyes. The article documents the collapse of visual verification systems as generative AI advances faster than detection methods, creating an epistemic crisis where even experts cannot reliably distinguish real from fabricated media within the timeframes that matter for social propagation.

key_entities: Hany Farid (digital forensics expert, UC Berkeley professor, co-founder GetReal Security)
Emily Cooper (vision scientist, UC Berkeley, Farid's wife, researches human perception)
Tech Giants (Silicon Valley companies developing generative AI systems)
Social Media Platforms (distribution infrastructure for deepfakes)
GetReal Security (Farid's company developing detection tools)
Dartmouth College (Farid's new institutional home as of July 2026)
North Korean Government Operatives (using deepfakes for employment fraud)
key_tensions: Creation speed vs detection speed (deepfakes generated in seconds, analysis takes hours/days)
Social media propagation velocity vs verification timeframes (90-second post half-life vs multi-hour analysis)
Profit-driven AI development vs societal safety (tech giants' incentives vs public interest)
Expert confidence erosion vs public reliance on expertise (Farid losing trust while being consulted more)
key_claims: Most people can no longer distinguish real photographs from AI-generated images (Farid's research finding)
Detection is costly and difficult while creation is easy, cheap, fast and reliable (student's summary, Farid confirms)
Within 20 minutes of posting, the damage is already done regardless of later verification (Farid's observation)
The visual system will be 'utterly useless' within 1-2 years (Farid's prediction)
Tech giants will 'burn everything to the ground as long as they're making a profit' (Farid's assessment)
Cross-modal consistency checking is the detection frontier (research literature finding)
Deepfake content grew roughly 900% over the past year (quantitative claim)
key_mechanisms: Social media propagation dynamics (90-second half-life, 20-minute saturation window)
Detection methodology (frame-by-frame analysis, shadow geometry, blood flow measurement, cross-modal consistency)
North Korean employment fraud pipeline (AI impersonation on Zoom → remote job → nuclear weapons funding)
key_absences: Regulatory framework or liability structure for deepfake creation/distribution
Platform-level verification systems operating at social media speed
Institutional response to the epistemic crisis beyond individual expert consultation

axiom_contradictions.basis: Indexical realism holds that the physics of light capture grounds recoverable truth; epistemic collapse holds that this grounding is irreversibly severed by generative AI. No framework can hold both that detection can restore verification capacity AND that the visual system is utterly useless.

Indexical realism grounds authority in physical indexicality; post-evidentiary denies that indexicality ever grounded authority (social consensus did). No framework can hold both that media are indexical traces AND that indexicality was never the source of evidentiary power.

Epistemic collapse holds that no verification method can succeed; distributed verification holds that cryptographic/consensus methods can succeed. No framework can hold both that verification is impossible AND that distributed verification works.

omegas.description: The Iran elementary school bombing video (150+ deaths, mostly children) is the article's central case study. Farid's analysis found 'no compelling evidence' of manipulation, but he remained uncertain. If the video was real, it represents a war crime; if fake, it represents successful deepfake propaganda. The article never resolves this, leaving the reader in the same epistemic uncertainty Farid experiences. This unresolved case may be the article's structural point.
omegas.source: Article narrative structure + F01 (Premise Drift) check

fracture_scan.notes: No fractures detected. Multi-lens scan drew from digital forensics, information epistemology, media theory, social constructivism, cryptography, and institutional analysis. Kernel/reading decomposition applied correctly: the topic IS a contested kernel (four distinct readings of visual evidentiary authority), not a set of independent axes. The readings pass the individually-holdable test and cannot be collapsed. Dark matter probes surfaced regulatory absence, platform verification gap, and the Cooper myopia parallel as omega material. The Iran bombing case study is deliberately unresolved in the source material, mirroring the epistemic crisis the article documents.
